statement: Finite curve quotient, finite etale scheme cover, injectivity of all inertia maps into etale pi1, and an ordinary analytic universal cover are equivalent for a smooth separated DM curve over Qbar.
notes: Behrend-Noohi Theorems4.2,4.4,1.1; Remark4.3; Proposition7.2; Corollary7.7. Scheme frame-torsor construction and comparison spelled out.

statement: For effective orbifold curves the only exceptions are P1 with one cone point or two unequal cone orders; each football has pi1=C_gcd(m,n) and explicitly noninjective inertia in the bad cases.
notes: Complete family-wise counterexample proof, not a representative-only example; effective hypothesis explicit.

statement: For arbitrary DM curves the extra exceptions are spherical gerbes whose weighted-projective universal cover is not P(1,1); the exact cases are listed by effective orbifold signature and cyclic kernel of generic inertia. P(n,n) is a bad gerbe for n>1.
notes: Behrend-Noohi Propositions7.4-7.6, Corollary7.7. Source misprint k corrected to d using its proof; final subgroup-generator slip repaired by a kernel of pi1(surface)->C_n. No statement depends on these slips.

statement: Existence of a finite etale curve cover over an algebraic closure descends to every characteristic-zero field after changing the cover and finite group. In particular existence descends from Qbar to Q.
notes: No field-of-moduli obstruction to existence: descend to finite L, compose the etale atlas, then take a frame torsor/Galois closure. Geometric connectedness of the cover is not asserted.

statement: For a smooth integral-base DM stack with relative normal-crossings boundary meeting every residue characteristic, every finite etale cover of the complement extends uniquely over the boundary.
notes: SGA1 XIII Proposition5.5 checked in original primary PDF; generic tameness forces every boundary ramification index prime to every p, hence1. X Theorem3.1 purity checked.

statement: pi1^et(M_1,1 over Z)=1. Nontrivial inertia therefore prevents every finite etale scheme atlas and every quotient presentation [C/G] with G constant finite.
notes: Full integral Weierstrass atlas W=A5-V(c4,Delta), connected coordinate-change group, purity, and Minkowski argument. Includes primes2 and3; not inferred from a Z[1/6] presentation.

statement: Over Z[1/3], M_1,1=[Y(3)/GL2(F3)] with group order48; fixed Weil-pairing geometric components have group SL2(F3) of order24.
notes: Bruin section4 explicit full-level3 construction and Theorem7.1 opened. Small-prime failure of this level cover is separated from C.6.

statement: The labelled schemes M_0,4 over Z and M_0,5 over Z both have trivial etale fundamental group.
notes: Explicit P1 and three-point blowup compactifications with relative SNC boundary. All-finite-prime arithmetic argument uses boundary sections; M04 need not have an integral point itself.

statement: The quotient stacks [M_0,4/S4] and [M_0,5/S5] over Z have etale fundamental groups S4 and S5. The four-point action has kernel V4, and its effective S3 quotient is a different stack. M_0,5 has dimension2.
notes: Constant finite groups are etale even when p divides their order; quotient atlas remains a torsor. Ineffective V4 is retained. Dimension corrects the curve wording for M05.

statement: Exact checks cover all144 ordered football pairs in the box1..12, all24 cross-ratio permutations, all120 five-point boundary permutations, GL2(F3), and the integral Weierstrass algebraic ingredients.
notes: All stated finite boxes exhausted; symbolic tangent determinant=-1 proves every residue characteristic at once. pi1 claims depend on proofs, not finite testing.
